budget_items.topic: Weston & Sampson stormwater utility feasibility study proposal
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force reviewed a new cost estimate from Weston and Sampson (successor to prior consultant CI) and said it "breaks the bank," prompting discussion of reducing the scope of work.
A member asked how much is left to spend on the storm water initiative; Bill said the demonstration BMP would draw further from that same pool, leaving little remaining.

Members questioned where CI's parcel counts came from, since the GIS database was updated more recently than CI's report; they discussed narrowing the number of parcels needing individual impervious-area review by excluding residential codes.
A member estimated that excluding residential parcels and other scope cuts to Task 3/Task 4 would save a meaningful amount.
Members discussed a target figure they are trying to reach for the overall consultant scope, referencing a number below what was originally proposed.
Members discussed whether bills should go out quarterly or twice a year to save printing/mailing cost, noting the per-bill amount would simply be larger if billed less often.

budget_items.topic: Revised total scope-of-work cost after cuts
budget_items.what_was_said: A member did quick math on cutting Task 6 meetings in half and eliminating Tasks 2 and 4, arriving at a reduced total to bring back to the Town Manager.

budget_items.topic: Comparison to prior consultant CI's pricing
budget_items.what_was_said: Members compared the new reduced estimate to what CI had charged for a comparable scope including BMP and storm water utility work.

budget_items.topic: Chapter 90 funds as possible funding source
budget_items.what_was_said: Rather than a special town meeting request, a member suggested transferring available Chapter 90 highway funds into the storm water study, noting the town may receive a larger Chapter 90 allocation this year that has not yet arrived.

budget_items.topic: Town budget capacity for the study
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the town's contact (Jen) does not have funds on hand to cover the study's cost either, reinforcing the need to reduce scope before returning to her.

decisions.decision: Modify Task 3 of the Weston & Sampson scope to exclude residential parcels (and related codes such as condos) from individual impervious-area review.
Remove Task 2 and Task 4 from the proposed scope of work, and reduce Task 6 to one small-group meeting, two public presentations, and five monthly progress meetings.
Take the reduced scope-of-work cost figure to the Town Manager before proceeding.
Explore transferring available Chapter 90 highway funds to cover the study cost rather than seeking money at a special town meeting.
Set up a call/Zoom with Weston & Sampson, with one or two task force members participating, to discuss reducing the scope of work.

Respond to the master plan steering committee's questionnaire identifying the storm water infrastructure fund item, and taking the position that storm water infrastructure also counts as a resiliency strategy for conservation land.
Produce a durable (tin/aluminum) sign for the storm water BMP kiosk describing what the demonstration BMP is and how it works, then hand the design off to be fabricated.
Set the next meeting date for October 16.

minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed a new, expensive scope-of-work proposal from consultant Weston & Sampson for a stormwater utility fee study and worked through cutting it down task by task -- excluding residential parcels from impervious-area assessment, dropping two tasks entirely, and reducing the number of public and progress meetings -- to bring a smaller cost figure back to the Town Manager. They also approved prior minutes by roll call, discussed funding the study via a Chapter 90 transfer instead of a special town meeting, gave input to the master plan steering committee, and set the next meeting for October 16.

what_happened.line: The task force cut tasks from Weston & Sampson's stormwater fee-study scope to bring a lower cost figure to the Town Manager.
Members voted to remove two tasks entirely and reduce public and progress meetings under Task 6.
Task 3 was narrowed to exclude residential and condo parcels from individual impervious-area review.
The task force will explore funding the study with a Chapter 90 highway-funds transfer instead of asking a special town meeting for money.
Prior meeting minutes were approved by roll call; the next meeting is set for October 16.

why_it_matters: This study is the first step toward a possible stormwater utility fee, a new charge that could appear on residents' bills.
Paying for the study through a Chapter 90 transfer, rather than a special town meeting, would keep that funding decision off a resident vote.
How Task 3 counts parcels -- residential included or excluded -- shapes who eventually gets assessed and billed under any future fee.
